reviewItems.title: Smaller phone, laptop makers dig in for years of memory scarcity
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: Device makers are facing acute DRAM scarcity; supplier bargaining power is high and industry participants expect tight memory supply to persist into 2027-2028.

reviewItems.title: Microchip reports first quarter fiscal 2027 financial results
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: Microchip reported sequential and year-on-year sales growth, improving end demand and inventory normalization, with guidance for further sequential growth.

reviewItems.title: Anglo-Teck wait shows mining M&A's rising toll
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: Copper had surged to a record around $14,700 per tonne, underscoring supply scarcity and the strategic value of high-quality copper assets.

reviewItems.title: Chile's state-owned miner Codelco says restructuring plan may be delayed until end of 2026
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: Codelco's current production goal had been revised down to about 1.3 million tonnes from a previously projected 1.7 million, while the miner faced stagnant production and rising costs.

reviewItems.title: US imports more Congo copper as consumer acceptance grows
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: US imports of DRC copper reached a record 53,290 tonnes in July and 23.9% of total US imports; industrial buyers increasingly accepted Congolese cathode sold at discounts to COMEX-approved brands.

reviewItems.title: Chinese MDI/TDI producers announce price increases
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: Major producers announced MDI/TDI price increases, but downstream purchasing remained cautious and the move appeared driven more by cost/supply discipline than broad end-demand acceleration.

reviewItems.title: Physical oil cargoes trade at extreme premiums amid disruptions
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: Physical crude/product markets showed severe short-term tightness and high cargo premiums, but the shock was heavily influenced by logistics/geopolitical disruptions.

reviewItems.title: Southern Co unit signs deal with Google to add nuclear capacity
reviewItems.normalizedClaim: Surging electricity demand from data centers is driving interest in expanding round-the-clock nuclear capacity, reinforcing the already widely recognized AI-power-demand theme.
